title: ConventionDeltas
description: Schema for forge ConventionLearner outputs (§7.11/§11.7, Task 3.2). Mirrors ConventionDeltas in forge-agents/Reviews.scala. `claudeMdProposal` is always present and nullable (an object when the learner proposes a CLAUDE.md edit, null otherwise) — expressed as anyOf{object|null} because Codex's --output-schema (OpenAI strict mode) forbids oneOf and requires every property in `required` (design-rationale C17).

addCommands.description: Gate commands the repo profile was MISSING that would have avoided an observed failure (e.g. a format autofix the run kept paying fix-up rounds for). Additive only — never propose removing or rewriting an existing command. Empty array if the profile already declares every command the failures needed.

claudeMdProposal.description: A proposed addition to the repo's own CLAUDE.md (a convention the run taught), or null if you have nothing worth proposing. NOT applied by Forge — persisted for a human to review and merge.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what the run's failures revealed and what you propose. Shown in the audit log.

argv.description: The command split into argv tokens, e.g. ['sbt', 'scalafmtAll'].

determinism.description: 'deterministic' = re-running is a pure function of the working tree (a formatter, codegen); 'heuristic' = interpreting the outcome needs judgment (a test could be a bug, a flake, or an env issue).

required.description: Whether this gate must pass before a change can merge.

autofix.description: True when running the command mutates the working tree to remediate the failure (a formatter rewrites files). Only deterministic + autofix commands are safe for Forge to run itself without a driver turn.

rationale.description: Why this convention is worth adding — the failure→remedy pattern you observed in this run.

suggestedAddition.description: The convention text to add to CLAUDE.md, phrased as a directive (e.g. 'The implement driver must run `sbt scalafmtAll` before settling').
